correctness.rationale: The primary complete independent-block facet theorem specializes on a block path to odd-length alternating +/-1 normals; the specialization is proved from its disjoint negative-gap requirements. Every inball center obeys lower endpoint clearances and two distinguished upper facet clearances with summed normals e1+en, giving rho*(2+||a||+||b||)<=2. Even and odd explicit centers satisfy every facet inequality by bounding support lengths and even-coordinate sums; equality proves both radius formulas. Three independent active equations constrain optimal centers to codimension three; explicitly constructed positive small perturbations make all other facets strict. All quantifiers n>=2 and n>=3, including n=2 square and n=3 unique-center boundary, are handled. The standalone checker reconstructs actual facets and LP centers, with finite results treated as corroborative only.

value.rationale: The zero-inclusive connected-block path polytope is a canonical and intrinsically motivated family: connected subgraph geometry, facets, Gorenstein structure, and Narayana h*-enumeration are established for it. The theorem gives its entire Euclidean inradius sequence, a genuine even/odd split in the optimal radius, and an unexpectedly large affine (n-3)-dimensional continuum of optimal centers rather than a single incenter. The double-facet endpoint certificate and complete incenter halfspace description isolate new geometric behavior not implied by the published lattice or facet enumeration data, beyond a dimension-specific numerical gain.
